sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Nutley, NJ?
sections.html:
Nutley is a small, dense township in Essex County, and every resale there needs a municipal Certificate of Occupancy before closing. You can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer, but all three routes pass through the same Nutley inspection step.

The township covers 3.37 square miles of land and borders Belleville and Bloomfield in Essex County, Lyndhurst in Bergen County and Clifton in Passaic County. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 30,744 residents, up from 30,143 at the 2020 census. With roughly 8,900 people per square mile, most houses sit close together on small lots, so a buyer looks hard at the roof, the sump pump and the basement.

sections.h2: How did Nutley develop, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The area grew out of the Satterthwaite estate, which gave the place its name, and out of mill and quarry work along the Third River. Brownstone quarrying in the Avondale section employed Italian and Irish immigrants, and the mills left street names behind. Nutley was set off from Belleville as Franklin Township in 1874, became a town in 1902 and became a township in 1981.

Older housing stock is the practical result. Many Nutley homes predate modern electrical and plumbing codes, which is why the transfer inspection looks closely at panels, venting and water heater piping. Sellers who finished a basement or attic years ago should check that a permit was closed out.

Nutley was also the U.S. base of Hoffmann-La Roche from 1929, and the company's roughly $9 million in local property taxes had made up about 9 percent of township tax revenue. Roche announced in 2012 that the site would close, with the shutdown slated for the end of 2015.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Nutley homes and buyers?
sections.html:
Seven in ten Nutley households own their home, and the median owner-occupied value is $516,300 for 2020 through 2024. That makes Nutley a steady owner-occupant market rather than a rental-driven one. The figures below come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for the township.

sections.h2: What does the Nutley Certificate of Occupancy inspection check?
sections.html:
The township code, Chapter 700, Article XVII, Section 700-116, requires a Certificate of Occupancy to be applied for and issued before a property is sold, conveyed or rented. The township describes it as a safety inspection and says it is in no way a home inspection. Items the inspectors list include:

  • Work done without permits, and any open building permits, which must be closed through final inspections first.
  • Smoke detection on every level including the basement near the stairs, plus detectors within 10 feet of each bedroom.
  • Carbon monoxide detectors outside bedrooms where the home has a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage.
  • Relief valves on the water heater and boiler piped to within 6 inches of the floor.
  • A sump pump, if present, discharging outside rather than into the sanitary sewer or onto a neighbor.
  • Handrails or guardrails on anything over four steps, intact stairs, and covers on every switch and outlet.
  • House numbers between 4 and 8 inches tall, visible from the street.

Illegal conversions and unpermitted living areas also draw attention. If you suspect an unpermitted bedroom or finished basement, ask the Code Enforcement Department before you list, because no Zoning Certificate is issued while a permit is open.

sections.h2: How do I schedule a transfer inspection in Nutley?
sections.html:
Start with the Code Enforcement Department on the second floor of the municipal building at 1 Kennedy Drive. Since July 1, 2026, inspection requests must be in writing, either through the township's online portal or on the request form, and they must reach the department at least 24 hours ahead.

  • Building and zoning transfer inspections run Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
  • Fire and zoning transfer inspections run Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
  • The Fire Department handles the smoke and carbon monoxide compliance application, so expect two stops rather than one.

State fire code also requires a smoke alarm compliance certificate before a one- or two-family home is sold, and the Division of Fire Safety says the certificate lasts six months from issue. Schedule the inspection close enough to closing that the certificate does not lapse, but early enough to repair anything that fails.

sections.h2: What other costs and filings come with a Nutley sale?
sections.html:
Sellers pay New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. The Division of Taxation's example puts the fee at $1,910 on a $325,000 deed with no exemption. Buyers pay an extra 1 percent fee on sales over $1,000,000, which rarely affects Nutley.

Every deed also needs a Gross Income Tax form from the seller. New Jersey residents sign the GIT/REP-3, while nonresident sellers use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 and may owe an estimated tax prepayment unless an assurance on the GIT/REP-3 applies.

If you think your assessment is too high, the petition goes to the Essex County board of taxation, which must receive it by April 1, or 45 days after assessment notices are mailed, whichever is later. The form states that only value can be appealed, not the tax bill, and evidence must be comparable sales rather than neighboring assessments.

sections.h2: Which Nutley roads, transit and schools affect buyer demand?
sections.html:
The Garden State Parkway clips the township's southwest corner, Route 7 runs along the north edge and Route 21 follows the eastern border. NJ Transit bus 192 goes to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and routes 13, 27, 72 and 74 reach Newark. Passenger rail ended in 1966, so the bus is the commuter link.

Nutley Public Schools run seven schools, with 4,034 students in 2021-22. The elementary schools are Lincoln, Radcliffe, Spring Garden, Washington and Yantacaw, followed by John H. Walker Middle School and Nutley High School. Franklin Avenue's shops and a chain of parks, including Memorial Park, Booth Park and Kingsland Park, round out what listing photos usually feature.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Nutley house?
sections.html:
A cash buyer fits best when the house needs work the Certificate of Occupancy would flag, when you inherited a property and want to avoid carrying costs, or when a closing date matters more than the last few thousand dollars of price. Ask any buyer who is purchasing as-is to confirm, in writing, who handles the township's inspection and any open permits.

Compare a cash offer against the net from a listing, after agent fees, repairs, the transfer fee and carrying costs. A written offer with a closing date you control is worth more than a verbal number.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Occupancy to sell a house in Nutley?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 700-116 of the Nutley code requires a Certificate of Occupancy to be applied for and issued before any property in the township is sold, conveyed or rented. Open building permits must be closed before the zoning certificate is issued.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I request a Nutley transfer inspection?
faqs.a: Give at least 24 hours, and more if repairs are likely. Inspection requests have had to be in writing since July 1, 2026, through the township portal or the request form. Fire and zoning inspections are offered only three days a week.

faqs.q: How long is a smoke alarm certificate good for in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Six months from the date of issue, according to the state Division of Fire Safety. A one- or two-family home needs the certificate before it can be sold, and the owner obtains it through the municipality.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Nutley property assessment?
faqs.a: The county board of taxation must receive the petition by April 1 of the tax year, or 45 days after the bulk mailing of assessment notices, whichever is later. A municipal-wide revaluation moves the date to May 1. Late petitions are dismissed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Nutley house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, but the inspection requirement does not disappear. The Certificate of Occupancy still has to be applied for, and any unpermitted work or missing detectors will be flagged. Settle in the contract who pays for corrections before closing.
